name: Traefik
description: Traefik reverse proxy reads over its API: the HTTP/TCP/UDP overview, HTTP routers, services, middlewares, entrypoints and the running version. Read-only; no dynamic-config write is wired here. The API is unauthenticated by default (base_url is the only credential); Traefik's own docs recommend fronting it with auth or restricting it to a trusted network for anything beyond local access.

tools.name: overview
tools.description: Get Traefik's overview: HTTP/TCP/UDP router and service counts, enabled features and configured providers

tools.name: list_http_routers
tools.description: List the configured HTTP routers with their rule, target service, status, entrypoints, provider and priority

tools.name: list_http_services
tools.description: List the configured HTTP services with their status, provider, type and backing server status

tools.name: list_http_middlewares
tools.description: List the configured HTTP middlewares with their status, provider and type

tools.name: list_entrypoints
tools.description: List the configured network entrypoints with their listen address

tools.name: version
tools.description: Get the running Traefik version, codename and release date

needs_review: AUTH IS none BY DESIGN: Traefik's API is unauthenticated once enabled ([api] insecure or api@internal), so base_url is the only credential and auth.type is 'none'. Fronting the API with basic auth or a trusted network is a deployment concern documented by Traefik, not a spec one.
READ-ONLY: all six tools are GET, write:false. The API has no dynamic-config write surface; static/dynamic configuration is file- or label-driven, not settable through this endpoint.
list_http_routers/services/middlewares return an empty array with a 200 on a fresh instance with no routers defined via labels or file provider yet; that is a valid live proof, not a failure.
list_entrypoints reflects only entrypoints declared at startup (e.g. --entrypoints.web.address=:80); a minimal container may expose just one, which is still a valid non-empty proof.
LIVE-PROOF CONTRACT: every tool takes no input, so every _probe is {}. Proven against docker traefik:v3.1, then destroyed.
